title: Object-typed OpenFeature flags need conditional JsonValue import in generated file
answers: Why does the generated openfeature react file sometimes import JsonValue and sometimes not?
How do object-valued flags get their TypeScript type in the generated hooks file?
body: Symptom: generated OpenFeature React file fails to typecheck/lint because it imports an unused type, or an object-valued flag's hook has no type for its default value. Root cause: the template previously had no notion of object-typed flags or their TS type. Fix pattern: template data now carries Flagset.HasObject (set true if any flag's Type == "object"); openfeature_react.tmpl conditionally imports `type JsonValue` from @openfeature/react-sdk only when HasObject is true, and object flags' hooks return JsonValue. Constraints: any future flag value shape added to the typed-flag mapping that needs a new TS type must follow this same opt-in import pattern to avoid unused imports when no flag of that type exists.

search: OpenFeature React hook generation in pkg/services/featuremgmt/openfeature_react.tmpl must conditionally import type JsonValue from @openfeature/react-sdk only when Flagset.HasObject is true, preventing unused-import typecheck/lint failures. Object-valued flags' hooks return JsonValue; non-object flag shapes bypass this import. Any future flag value type added to the typed-flag mapping must follow the same conditional opt-in pattern for the import to avoid unused types when that flag shape doesn't exist in a given flagset.
